messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing intermittent packet loss between gpu-pool nodes in us-east-1 (zone-a -> zone-b). Pulses last ~10-30s, every ~5-15m. GRPC streams hit RTOs and a few client reconnects.

sam: same here. Envoy metrics show connect failures and ~250ms tail latencies during pulses. Not continuous, very bursty.

jake: I grabbed a tcpdump during one pulse. Lots of retransmits and repeated UDP GENEVE packets. snippet:```17:42:12.123456 IP 10.0.12.5.45678 > 10.0.34.7.6081: UDP, length 1180
17:42:12.123789 IP 10.0.34.7.6081 > 10.0.12.5.45678: UDP, length 1180
--- many duplicates / retransmits ---```

infra-bot: alert: route /v1/stream-ingress error rate 3.8x baseline for 00:02:00 (us-east-1 gpu-pool). Ticket created #INFRA-4921.

olivia: any recent infra changes in that AZ? kernel/driver/firmware?

maria: Kernel bump to 5.10.92 two days ago on the gpu-pool nodes. Also pushed a small cilium config change (encap=true) last night but rolled back at 03:00.

raj: can we check NIC offloads (GRO/GSO/TSO) and MTU consistency? those often bite with encap.

sam: ran a quick mtud and ping:```ping -s 1400 10.0.34.7
--- 10.0.34.7 ping statistics ---
5 packets transmitted, 4 received, 20% packet loss, time 4004ms
```

jake: ethtool -k on a node:```tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
gso: on
gro: on
```

olivia: if GSO/GRO interact badly with geneve encap we can see bursts or broken offload leading to retransmits. Any mlx5 firmware updates recently?

maria: vendor pushed mlx5 FW v18.25 two days ago with the kernel bump.

sam: hypothesis: firmware + kernel + encap (GENEVE) path causes occasional buffer/segmentation in NIC offload -> packets dropped then retransmitted. Matches bursty, short pulses.

raj: quick mitigation: disable GSO/GRO on host NICs for gpu-pool for an hour and monitor. Cost is some CPU but may stabilize. Who can run? @jake?

jake: I'll run a canary: disable offloads on 2 nodes and run load. command:```sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off```I’ll also run iperf and a pprof load against model-serving to try to reproduce.

maria: also please validate MTU across host <-> switch <-> tunnel. Our encap + inner MTU should be consistent: host MTU 1500, geneve adds ~50-80 bytes. Recommend host MTU 9000 on gpu hosts in that AZ to avoid fragmentation.

sam: note: we also saw small heartbeats on the underlay switches about interface buffer spikes during the times. Eng-net has been looking at that too.

olivia: opened a vendor support case with Mellanox, included tcpdumps and pcap. Case #MLX-7382.

raj: plan: (1) Jake canary offload disable on 2 nodes now, (2) increase sample logging for envoy and cilium trace headers, (3) infra team coordinate with network on underlay buffer spikes, (4) if stable after 30m roll to rest of affected pool, (5) keep vendor case open for FW fix.

maria: assigned to jake, sam for monitoring. tagging oncall: @raj if we need cross-AZ mitigation. :thumbsup:

jake: canary started at 18:10. Running sustained GRPC load at 80% baseline. will report back in 20m.

sam: pushed a dashboard panel for per-node retransmits + envoy RTOs and a short alert if >3 nodes hit >2% retransmit in 5m.

infra-bot: update: CANARY run (nodes gpu-canary-01/02) started by jake at 1784568200.

jake: initial 15m looks promising — no pulses on canary nodes yet, CPU up ~12% but stable.

maria: good. if sustained we'll schedule a controlled rollout. Also keep eye on RDMA workloads — if people use RoCE it's a different stack.

olivia: vendor flagged a known interaction between FW v18.25 and Linux 5.10 with encap; suggested a driver param workaround: "mlx5_core.disable_tso=1" until FW patch. They recommended disabling host TSO/GSO as we did.

raj: ok plan accepted. I'll update INFRA-4921 with actions and timeline. Thanks team.

maria: follow-ups: (a) postmortem if incident recurs after rollback, (b) include perf delta and cost impact for disabling offloads, (c) schedule firmware patch window with vendor once available.

sam: noted. closing loop after 2h monitoring.
